findings.title: VarianceController silently drops Float32 precision through a bare Float64 literal, on the path every default Simulation now takes
findings.before: (no prior code — VarianceController is new in this round)
findings.after:
const _DISSIPATION_GROUP = 0.9
_stationary_dissipation_estimate(k, L) = (k / _DISSIPATION_GROUP)^(3 / 2) / L
...
  tℓ = turnover_time === nothing ?
       2 * float(target) / (3 * _stationary_dissipation_estimate(float(target), domain.grid.domain_size[1])) :
       float(turnover_time)
...
  return VarianceController(band, promote(float(target), float(gain), tℓ)...)
findings.why_it_matters: Verified by direct execution: VarianceController(domain; target = Float32(1.5)) on a Float32 FixedDomain — and, since this struct is now the default velocity_forcing, a plain Simulation(domain) on a Float32 domain — yields VarianceController{K, Float64} (target/gain/relaxation_time all promoted to Float64), because _DISSIPATION_GROUP = 0.9 is a bare Float64 literal that the turnover_time===nothing default path always divides by, and promote(...) then upcasts the whole struct once any one component is Float64. This happens even with an explicit gain = Float32(1.0) — only supplying turnover_time explicitly avoids it. It is exactly the defect class test/regressions/r4-free-modules-04-target-factor-float64.jl exists to catch elsewhere ("A Float64 literal breaks that match on a Float32 run"), and the very same file's own _target_factor comment states the house rule this violates: use an Int/Rational, never a floating literal, "off a Float32 run's element type ... which the rest of the observable surface is pinned to preserve." No test in this round exercises VarianceController on a Float32 domain, so the regression is unnoticed by the suite. It doesn't crash — the amplitude is cast back to T before touching any array — but it silently violates the project's own stated precision-as-fitness-axis invariant on the strategy that is now the default for every run.

findings.title: The run layer's DEFAULT forcing changed from an exact per-step clamp to a soft feedback controller, changing the numeric behavior of every prior default-configured Simulation
findings.before: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),
findings.why_it_matters: BandRescaling(over=:total) deterministically forced the whole-field kinetic energy to equal kinetic_energy at the end of every single step (an algebraic constraint); VarianceController only relaxes toward it exponentially with a settling time t_ℓ/G, leaving a genuine, gain-dependent fluctuation around the target. Any caller who built a Simulation(...) without an explicit velocity_forcing — the documented, front-door default — now gets a different trajectory and a k that is no longer pinned exactly to the requested value (the accompanying test in test/simulation_run.jl was loosened from an implicit exact hold to rtol = 0.05/0.1 checks). This is presented, tested and reasoned as an order-of-accuracy fix (the old default silently ran at first order on a third-order scheme) and decision 58 records it as user-directed, but it is nonetheless the highest-blast-radius behavior change in the round: it silently redefines what "forced and stationary by default" delivers for every existing caller of the unmodified front door.

findings.title: ConstantPower's rate-application route changed, altering the computed trajectory of every existing ConstantPower-forced run
findings.before:
function set_forcing_rate!(forcing::ConstantPower, rate, field, domain::FixedDomain)
  T = field_scalar_type(rate)
  band_observable = _target_factor(field) * weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)  # KE_band or variance_band (fused)
  amplitude = _band_is_empty(band_observable) ? 0.0 :
              forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)
  rate .= T(amplitude) .* forcing.indicator
  return rate
end
uses_linear_rate(::ConstantPower) = true
findings.after:
function add_forcing_source!(forcing::ConstantPower, N̂, field, domain::FixedDomain,
                             diffusivity::Real)
  T = field_scalar_type(N̂)
  band_observable = _target_factor(field) * weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)   # at the STAGE state
  amplitude = _injection_amplitude(forcing.injection_rate, band_observable)
  convolve!(N̂, field, forcing.band, T(amplitude), one(T))
  return N̂
end
uses_steady_linear_rate(::ConstantPower) = false
findings.why_it_matters: ConstantPower used to fold a rate frozen at the step's start into the exact integrating factor; it now re-evaluates the rate at every Runge–Kutta stage as an additive source. For the same injection_rate, RNG seed and grid, an existing simulation built with ConstantPower now integrates a numerically different trajectory step-by-step (only converging to the same continuum limit as Δt→0). The change is well-motivated (the old route silently collapsed the scheme to first order) and is heavily tested, but it is a silent change to a computed result for input that previously ran and produced specific numbers — worth flagging as exactly the kind of alteration the audit is watching for, independent of whether the new numbers are "more correct."

findings.title: The accuracy fix triples-plus the default configuration's per-step host-readback cost, and the round defers rather than closes the resulting gap
findings.before:
(name = "default (adaptive dt, BandRescaling :total)",
   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :band_total),                 achieved = 3, floor = 1),
findings.after:
(name = "default (adaptive dt, VarianceController, 3-stage)",
   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :controller, stages = 3),     achieved = 10, floor = 1),
findings.why_it_matters: The default run's blocking device→host synchronization count per step jumps from 3 (against a floor of 1) to 10 — the "largest gap in this ledger," per the added comment, which the round explicitly leaves open ("held, not accepted: the three per-stage reductions are one fused multi-weight reduction away") rather than closing in the same commit. This rides on the pre-existing generic HOST_SIDE_FORCING_SCALARS holder rather than being weighed on its own: a >3x increase on precisely the synchronization axis the package's GPU-primary invariant ("minimal footprint trumps compute cost") foregrounds is a real cost being paid for the correctness fix, and CLAUDE.md's own self-guard warns against treating a recorded-but-unbounded cost as thereby acceptable. Not a defect in the fix itself, but the round trades one invariant (temporal order) for pressure on another (GPU-primary minimal synchronization) without narrowing that new gap or asking whether 3 separate per-stage reductions were the cheapest way to get the corrected physics.

findings.title: The decision-log entry that records the fix states the formula it says was the bug
findings.before: The same diff writes the CORRECT law into src/Forcing.jl, twice — docstring: `A(\boldsymbol{\kappa}, t) = \frac{\varepsilon(t) - G[k(t) - k_\infty]/t_\ell}{2k_f(t)}`, and code: `restoring = forcing.gain * (whole_variance - forcing.target) / forcing.relaxation_time` with `whole_variance = factor * inner(field, field)   # k, the quantity held`.
findings.after: Decision 58, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1907 — `+    Moin (2016, Eq. 20): ``A = [\varepsilon - G(k_f - k_\infty)/t_\ell]/(2k_f)``, whose marginal term` `+    ``\varepsilon/2k_f`` reinjects exactly what dissipation removes and whose proportional term gives` `+    ``\mathrm dk/\mathrm dt = -G(k - k_\infty)/t_\ell``` — k_f, the BAND variance, in the restoring term.
findings.why_it_matters: The same entry's own postscript says: 'The first implementation put the *band* variance in both places of that formula — normalizing by ``k_f`` (right) and restoring toward ``k_f`` (wrong)… the run held the band at 1.5 and let k settle about 30% above it, silently breaking the grid-mode ν calibration.' The formula the entry publishes is that wrong version, and it is self-inconsistent: with k_f in the numerator the stated consequence dk/dt = −G(k−k_∞)/t_ℓ does not follow. I verified the code is right (measured dk/dt vs −G(k−k_∞)/t_ℓ agree to ratio 1.00000), so this is the authoritative record — the append-only decision log the project forbids re-litigating — carrying the defect a reader would reimplement from it.

findings.title: The default forcing was swapped, so every previously valid default run now computes different numbers and `kinetic_energy` is no longer an exact invariant
findings.before: `-                    velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),`
findings.after: `+                    velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),`
findings.why_it_matters: Measured, 400 default steps at 32^3 seeded identically: at base k−1.5 is exactly 0.0 at steps 1/5/20 and ±2.2e−16 at 100/400; at head it is −5.4e−7 → −2.5e−5 and monotonically growing, and the two final velocity fields differ from byte 1. Anyone with a default `Simulation(...)` gets a different trajectory and a different meaning for the `kinetic_energy` keyword — an exact per-step clamp became an exponential attractor with a 2.9-time-unit settling time. The defect actually demonstrated was ConstantPower's *routing* (uses_linear_rate on a state-dependent rate); swapping the front-door default and adding a whole new strategy is a strictly larger change riding along with it. It is disclosed in the docstring and pinned by a new test, which is why I mark it unclear rather than unjustified — but the diff nowhere states that the default's numerical output changes for existing users.

findings.title: The default step got 28.5% slower and issues 10 device readbacks where it issued 3 — and the ledger that measures that was re-baselined in the same commit onto an untouched holder
findings.before: `-  (name = "default (adaptive dt, BandRescaling :total)",` `-   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :band_total),                 achieved = 3, floor = 1),`
findings.after: `+  (name = "default (adaptive dt, VarianceController, 3-stage)",` `+   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :controller, stages = 3),     achieved = 10, floor = 1),` — with the comment `+ Ten crossings against a floor of one is the largest gap in this ledger, and it is held, not accepted`.
findings.why_it_matters: Measured at 64^3: default 35.35 → 45.44 ms/step (+28.5%); per-step `step!` allocation 2080 → 6336 B (3.05x, against a stated invariant that the hot loop is allocation-free over preallocated buffers); the compute ledger's forcing cell went from 3 spectral-vector passes per step to 6*3 = 18. On a GPU-primary package a 3→10 blocking readback jump in the DEFAULT hot loop is the headline cost of this change, and it is absorbed entirely by the pre-existing `HOST_SIDE_FORCING_SCALARS` holder whose text this diff does not touch — no new `:DESIGN` holder citing decision 58, and `OPEN_LOCAL_WINS` still empty. The project's own rule is that a recorded cost with no lower bound held against it is an unexamined cost; here the record was widened to fit the new number.

findings.title: The `VarianceRescaling` order claim is quantified over 'every other forcing in the module'; StochasticOU measures 0.126

findings.after: `+    is first-order however good the scheme is. Measured on the third-order `IFLowStorageRK3`: **1.02**` `+    here against **3.01** for every other forcing in the module.`

NoForcing 3.006, Linear 3.005, ConstantPower 3.006, VarianceController 3.005 — and StochasticOU 0.126, which is also 'in the module' (defined, docstringed, and carried in docs/docstring_shape.csv, merely un-exported). findings.title: The new `VarianceController` documents a constructor that cannot produce the object its own `# Fields` section describes
findings.before: Every sibling strategy documents the domain-taking form, e.g. `VarianceRescaling(domain; target, over, lowest_shell = 1, highest_shell = 2)`, and `DeferredForcing`'s docstring lists the operator-free forms: `Linear(; rate, …)` / `ConstantPower(; injection_rate, …)` / `+    VarianceRescaling(; target, over, lowest_shell = 1, highest_shell = 2)`.
findings.after: `+    VarianceController(; target, gain = 1.0, turnover_time = nothing,` `+                       lowest_shell = 1, highest_shell = 2)` … `+# Fields` `+- `band` — the band-pass kernel, lazy; …` `+- `target`, `gain`, `relaxation_time` — ``k_\infty``, ``G`` and ``t_\ell``.` — attached to `+struct VarianceController{K, T} <: AbstractForcing`.
findings.why_it_matters: I ran the documented call verbatim. `VarianceController(; target = 1.5, gain = 1.0, turnover_time = nothing, lowest_shell = 1, highest_shell = 2)` returns a `DeferredForcing`, and `.band`, `.target`, `.gain`, `.relaxation_time` each throw `FieldError: type DeferredForcing has no field …, available fields: build`. The docstring is the only surface a user reads (`?VarianceController`, the API page), it is the one strategy in the module whose header shows the deferred form, and the `domain` form the sim actually builds is documented nowhere — `domain` is also absent from its `# Arguments` list, which every sibling includes. `DeferredForcing`'s own catalogue of operator-free constructors was extended for the rename but not for the new strategy.

findings.title: The rename of `apply_forcing!` and `BandRescaling`, and the 3→5 arity change on the source hook, break third-party code beyond what the defect required
findings.before: `-  BandRescaling,` `-  uses_linear_rate,` `-  apply_forcing!,`
findings.after: `+  VarianceRescaling,` `+  VarianceController,` `+  uses_steady_linear_rate,` `+  project_forcing!,`
findings.why_it_matters: Executed at HEAD: `BandRescaling`, `apply_forcing!` and `uses_linear_rate` are all `UndefVarError`, and a base-era user forcing defining the old three-argument hook now makes `ResolvedGenerator` throw. Only one of these is argued from the defect: `uses_linear_rate` → `uses_steady_linear_rate` carries the load-bearing property the bug was about. `apply_forcing!` → `project_forcing!` and `BandRescaling` → `VarianceRescaling` are naming preferences bundled into an accuracy fix, and the arity change forces every implementer to rewrite even where both new arguments are ignored — the diff's own `StochasticOU` method is `add_forcing_source!(ou, N̂, field, domain, diffusivity) = add!(N̂, N̂, ou.state)   # the increment was drawn once per step; the stage field is not needed`. The package allows breaking changes, so this is a proportionality point, not a violation: four public breaks landed where one was demonstrated.

findings.title: The two instruments that would have priced this change were themselves edited by it — one self-admittedly, one left pointing at the retired path
findings.before: `-const POWER = measure(ConstantPower(DOMAIN; injection_rate = 1.0),        :rate)` `-vector_passes(c) = c.inner + c.weighted_inner + 2 * c.convolve` `-  return c`
findings.after: `+const POWER      = measure(ConstantPower(DOMAIN; injection_rate = 1.0),            :source)` `+source_passes(m)  = readbacks(m) + 3 * m.out.convolve` `+  # That is exactly how this test went vacuous when the state-dependent forcings moved to the source` `+  # hook (2026-08-22): the term it was written to measure quietly stopped being measured.`
findings.why_it_matters: The forcing-traffic witness returned only the input double, so after the move its `convolve` counter read zero and the pass comparison balanced at 0 == 0; the same commit that caused that repaired it and added its own 'the measurement is not vacuous' guard. That is the self-certifying shape: the oracle was corrected by the party it was auditing, and only its author's diligence, not the harness, closed it. Worse, the one frozen *allocation* budget in the suite (test/regressions/05-test-critic-05.jl, the `step! + deposit!` bytes guard) received a pure rename — `-velocity_forcing = BandRescaling(domain; target = 0.6, over = :band,` → `+velocity_forcing = VarianceRescaling(domain; …` — and so still exercises the retired forcing. I measured what it therefore never sees: the new default allocates 6336 B/step at 64^3 against 2080 B for the forcing the witness does test.

findings.title: The quoted 'measured' convergence orders do not reproduce to the digits given
findings.before: (new comment block; the base file carried no measurement)
findings.after: `+# Measured on IFLowStorageRK3 (third order), refinement ladder: NoForcing 2.995, Linear 2.987,` `+# ConstantPower 1.018 and VarianceRescaling 1.023 BEFORE this split` — echoed in test/integrators.jl (`ConstantPower 1.018, the front-door default 1.023, against 2.995 unforced`), test/memory_audit.jl (`measured 1.018 against 2.995 unforced`) and test/optimality_audit.jl (`measured collapsing IFLowStorageRK3 from 2.995 to 1.018`).

The finding is fully confirmed in direction and magnitude — third order collapses to first — but none of the four published figures reproduces, so they were taken from some other configuration that the diff does not state. findings.title: The rate predicate's meaning was widened from a checkable property to an unchecked one; the guard that enforces it was not extended
findings.before: `uses_linear_rate(::AbstractForcing) = false` — "Whether `forcing` drives its field through a linear per-mode rate — that is, whether it implements [`set_forcing_rate!`](@ref). The default is `false`; a forcing that does implement the hook **must** declare it `true`."
findings.after: `uses_steady_linear_rate(::AbstractForcing) = false` — "Whether `forcing` drives its field through a per-mode rate that is **constant in time** … *Steady*, not merely linear, is the load-bearing word: a per-mode rate re-solved from the state each step must **not** declare this."  `_overrides_rate_hook` in src/Generator.jl is unchanged and still asks only "does it define a method?"
findings.why_it_matters: At base the predicate was purely mechanical ("implements the hook"), and `_overrides_rate_hook` checked it in both directions, so the declaration could not lie. Head adds a second, semantic conjunct — steadiness in time — and adds a guard for the *other* hook's arity (`_defines_stale_source_hook`), but nothing checks the new conjunct. I built the witness: a user strategy `MyPower` that is literally the pre-fix `ConstantPower` (state-dependent A, `uses_steady_linear_rate(::MyPower) = true`). `Simulation(...; velocity_forcing = d -> MyPower(d; injection_rate = 0.2))` constructs without complaint, `generator.velocity_rate !== nothing` (it is handed a rate array and rides the integrating factor), and the measured temporal order is **1.045** against **3.006** for the shipped `ConstantPower` on the same 16³ grid, ν = 0.05, IFLowStorageRK3, seed 7. That is the exact defect this round removed from the package, still reachable by any user strategy, and silent — the run completes and reports nothing wrong. The docstring even writes the rule as a **must**; the code enforces nothing.

findings.title: The docstring accretion ratchet was reset in the same commit as the growth, and a rename bypasses its hard cap entirely
findings.before: `Forcing.jl::add_forcing_source!(forcing， N̂， domain) -> N̂,39,0,44`  /  `Forcing.jl::BandRescaling(domain; target， over， lowest_shell = 1， highest_shell = 2),54,3,600`  /  `Forcing.jl::uses_linear_rate(forcing) -> Bool,72,0,107`  /  `Forcing.jl::ConstantPower(…),91,1,376`  /  `SimulationRun.jl::Simulation(…),77,1,1688`
findings.after: `Forcing.jl::add_forcing_source!(forcing， N̂， field， domain， diffusivity) -> N̂,122,1,187`  /  `Forcing.jl::VarianceRescaling(…),86,1,679`  /  `Forcing.jl::uses_steady_linear_rate(forcing) -> Bool,72,0,166`  /  `Forcing.jl::ConstantPower(…),67,1,382`  /  `SimulationRun.jl::Simulation(…),77,1,1705`
findings.why_it_matters: `lint_docstring_shape()` (docs/make.jl 126–135) applies the growth ratchet only when `haskey(base, key)` and the hard caps `SHAPE_NEW_PARAGRAPH_CAP = 120` / `SHAPE_NEW_ADMONITION_CAP = 3` only when it does not. Two holes are exercised here at once. (a) `add_forcing_source!`'s longest paragraph went 39 → **122 words, above the 120-word hard cap for a new docstring** — it passes only because the CSV was regenerated in the same commit, which turns the new key into a known one and skips the cap branch forever. (b) The ratchet is keyed on the signature string, so every rename resets it: `BandRescaling` (600 words — the very docstring CLAUDE.md and docs/make.jl name as the cautionary example, cut down from 861) reappears as `VarianceRescaling` at **679**, +13%, with no baseline to fail against; `uses_linear_rate` 107 → `uses_steady_linear_rate` **166**, +55%. And three keys that did *not* change name grew anyway (ConstantPower 376→382, Linear 161→171, Simulation 1688→1705) and would each have failed `words > bw` — the wholesale re-baseline banked all of it. docs/make.jl's own instruction is "when a docstring legitimately grows, rewrite it whole rather than raise its number; when it *shrinks*, re-baseline". This re-baselined in the direction the guard exists to prevent.

findings.title: The frozen sync ledger for the default run was re-baselined from 3 to 10 readbacks under a pre-existing holder, while ARCHITECTURE.md still records three
findings.before: `(name = "default (adaptive dt, BandRescaling :total)",\n   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :band_total),                 achieved = 3, floor = 1),`
findings.after: `(name = "default (adaptive dt, VarianceController, 3-stage)",\n   cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :controller, stages = 3),     achieved = 10, floor = 1),`  — and `ALL_HOLDERS` / `OPEN_LOCAL_WINS = ()` are untouched
findings.why_it_matters: On the GPU-primary target the default configuration's blocking device-to-host readbacks per step went 3 → 10 against an unchanged floor of 1 — the largest gap in the ledger, a 3.3× regression on the hot loop — and the suite accepts it because the no-unclaimed-gap test (line 394: `@test s.floor > 0 || (s.holder !== nothing && s.holder in ALL_HOLDERS)`) only requires *a* holder to exist, and `HOST_SIDE_FORCING_SCALARS` already did. No new holder, no new `:FIX` entry, no `OPEN_LOCAL_WINS` addition. CLAUDE.md requires a deliberate step-schedule change to update the frozen ledgers "citing the decision", and decision 58 does not mention the readback cost at all. Worse, the same commit renamed but did not correct docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1365, which still reads "the default configuration issues **three** blocking readbacks per step — the CFL speed bound, and `VarianceRescaling`'s band and whole-field observables — against a floor of **one**", naming a forcing that is no longer the default. The architecture record and the ledger in one commit disagree by 3.3×, and the commit titled "the docs still described the defect, not the fix" left it.

findings.title: decision 58 records the wrong formula — the exact category error its own postscript says was the shipped bug
findings.before: (same entry, added in the same commit) "The first implementation put the *band* variance in both places of that formula — normalizing by ``k_f`` (right) and restoring toward ``k_f`` (wrong). … the run held the band at ``1.5`` and let ``k`` settle about 30% above it"
findings.after: (line 1907) "Moin (2016, Eq. 20): ``A = [\\varepsilon - G(k_f - k_\\infty)/t_\\ell]/(2k_f)``, whose marginal term ``\\varepsilon/2k_f`` reinjects exactly what dissipation removes and whose proportional term gives ``\\mathrm dk/\\mathrm dt = -G(k - k_\\infty)/t_\\ell``"
findings.why_it_matters: The code is right — `restoring = gain * (whole_variance - target) / relaxation_time` with `whole_variance = factor * inner(field, field)` (src/Forcing.jl:593–600) — and so is the Forcing.jl docstring's display formula, which reads ``[\\varepsilon(t) - G[k(t) - k_\\infty]/t_\\ell]/(2k_f(t))``. But §11 decision 58, the normative record a future reader is told not to re-litigate, states the restoring term over ``k_f``, which is the wrong physics the postscript three paragraphs later describes as having nearly shipped; the ``dk/dt`` identity quoted immediately after does not follow from the formula as written. The same slip recurs in the docstring's own identity sentence: "The rate is the marginal law ``A = \\varepsilon/2k``" (src/Forcing.jl:495) where the code and the display block use ``2k_f``. Of the three places this commit wrote the k / k_f distinction, one is right, one is wrong, and one is ambiguous — for a distinction the same commit says is invisible to the test suite and worth 30% in the held quantity.

findings.title: The sync model gained a `stages` parameter whose default silently under-prices exactly the forcings that changed
findings.before: `function _syncs(; adaptive_dt::Bool, velocity_forcing::Symbol, scalar_forcing::Symbol = :none,\n                  turnover_budget::Bool = false, monitor::Symbol = :none)`
findings.after: `function _syncs(; adaptive_dt::Bool, velocity_forcing::Symbol, scalar_forcing::Symbol = :none,\n                  turnover_budget::Bool = false, monitor::Symbol = :none, stages::Int = 1)` — with the ledger comment "`stages` is not optional here — a state-dependent forcing is evaluated at every stage, and a row that omits it silently prices the forcing as if it were armed once per step, which is the arrangement this whole round replaced."
findings.why_it_matters: The comment states the hazard precisely and then leaves the default at 1 with nothing enforcing it. A future SYNC_LEDGER row written `velocity_forcing = :controller` without `stages` freezes 4 crossings instead of 10 and the whole suite is content — the same shape of drift ("a cell that prices a per-stage cost as a per-step one") that this round was written to remove. Contrast the compute model, which has no such escape: `_forcing_pass_delta` hard-codes `6 * _evals(scheme)` inside the branch, so the stage count cannot be omitted. The two instruments over the same change were given opposite defaults, and only the strict one is safe.

findings.title: The one test that ties the sync model to executed code was rewritten to compare at stages = 1, leaving the 3× multiplier — the entire ledger change — verified by nothing
findings.before: `model_syncs(tag) = count(s -> occursin("(velocity)", s.site),\n                         OptModel._syncs(; adaptive_dt = false, velocity_forcing = tag))`  …  `@test model_syncs(:power)      == readbacks(POWER)`
findings.after: `model_syncs(tag; stages = 1) = count(…, OptModel._syncs(; adaptive_dt = false, velocity_forcing = tag, stages))`  …  `# ONE stage's worth, which is what \`measure\` exercises; the model multiplies by the stage count.`  `@test model_syncs(:power;      stages = 1) == readbacks(POWER)`  `@test model_syncs(:controller; stages = 1) == readbacks(CONTROLLER)`
findings.why_it_matters: This file exists precisely to stop the frozen models drifting from what the hooks do — its own header says the models "report FEWER host readbacks … than the code performs". Base asserted the model's number against measured reductions, and the model's number was the ledger's number. Head pins the model at `stages = 1` while the ledger row it certifies uses `stages = 3`, so the per-stage shape is checked and the multiplier that took the default from 3 to 10 is not checked at all. The sibling assertion in the same testset shows it could have been done: `@test model_vector_passes(:power) == EVALS_RK3 * source_passes(POWER)` does carry the multiplier. findings.title: The default forcing model was swapped, so every default `Simulation` now integrates different physics — and the exact k-hold the grid-mode ν calibration depends on became an asymptotic one, while the docs kept asserting it
findings.before: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),   ...  !!! note "The default holds the kinetic energy fixed, so it is not a measurable of the default run"  /  `BandRescaling` is a deterministic clamp: it rescales the band every step to hold the kinetic energy at the target **value**  ...  One precondition: the choice is self-consistent only if the run really holds ``k`` at `kinetic_energy`, which the front door's `BandRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees and `:band` does not.
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),   ...  !!! note "The default drives the kinetic energy to a set value, so read it as a control target"  /  `VarianceController` restores ``k`` exponentially to `kinetic_energy`  ...  The default `VarianceController` does — its restoring term measures the whole-field ``k`` — which is what makes this calibration legitimate.
findings.why_it_matters: Any script that calls `Simulation(grid_points_per_axis = N)` and takes the default forcing now runs a different physical model: a Bassenne feedback controller (with two new author-defaulted parameters, `gain = 1.0` and a derived `turnover_time`) instead of a per-step rescale. Under the old default the whole-field k was equal to `kinetic_energy` exactly after every step; now it only relaxes toward it with settling time t_ℓ/G, and the change set's own new test accepts `rtol = 0.05` after 200 steps. Grid mode solves ν from the ASSUMED k, so the resolution criterion κ_max·η that was exactly self-consistent is now self-consistent to within the controller's fluctuation (a 5% error in k propagates as ~7.5% in ε and ~2% in η). Trajectories, spectra, Re_λ and every fluctuation statistic of k differ from the previous default for identical inputs and seeds. The order defect that motivates the swap is real (a post-step rescale is Lie–Trotter and cannot be third order), but the docstring was rewritten from a guarantee ("guarantees") to a weaker mechanism while still being presented as making the calibration "legitimate" — the contract was restated to match the new behaviour rather than the loss being called out.

findings.title: `ConstantPower` moved from the integrating factor to the per-stage source: every existing ConstantPower run computes a different trajectory, at 3× the host readbacks and 12× the field passes on that axis
findings.before:
uses_linear_rate(::ConstantPower) = true

function set_forcing_rate!(forcing::ConstantPower, rate, field, domain::FixedDomain)
  T = field_scalar_type(rate)
  band_observable = _target_factor(field) * weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)
  amplitude = _band_is_empty(band_observable) ? 0.0 : forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)
  rate .= T(amplitude) .* forcing.indicator
  return rate
end
findings.after:
uses_steady_linear_rate(::ConstantPower) = false

function add_forcing_source!(forcing::ConstantPower, N̂, field, domain::FixedDomain,
                             diffusivity::Real)
  T = field_scalar_type(N̂)
  band_observable = _target_factor(field) * weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)   # at the STAGE state
  amplitude = _injection_amplitude(forcing.injection_rate, band_observable)
  convolve!(N̂, field, forcing.band, T(amplitude), one(T))
  return N̂
end
findings.why_it_matters: A user with an existing `ConstantPower` run gets different numbers: the forcing was applied through the exact exponential `exp((A − D|κ|²)τ)` with A frozen at the step start, and is now an explicit additive term evaluated afresh at each Runge–Kutta stage. The injected-power identity ⟨u·f⟩ = ε_target is preserved (verified algebraically), but the discrete trajectory is not. The cost moved with it: the change set's own re-frozen ledgers price the velocity slot at `_ex(spectral_vector = 4 * _evals(scheme))` = 12 field-scale vector passes per RK3 step where the base priced `_ex(spectral_vector = 1, …)`, and the sync ledger row goes `achieved = 2` → `achieved = 4`. The underlying order defect is genuine, but the narrower fix — re-arming the rate at each stage, keeping the exponential and one reduction per stage — is not considered or recorded anywhere in the change set, so no bound was produced showing the chosen route is the cheapest correct one.

findings.title: The new stale-hook guard rejects third-party forcings the run can call correctly — verified, twice, against the real package

findings.title: `VarianceController` refuses `gain = 0`, foreclosing the marginal-law limit its own docstring describes

findings.after: `(isfinite(gain) && gain > 0) || throw(ArgumentError("`gain` must be finite and positive, got $gain: a non-positive gain makes the restoring term push the variance AWAY from the target"))` (src/Forcing.jl:552–555); and `(isfinite(target) && target > 0) || throw(…)` (550).
findings.why_it_matters: `gain = 0` is not "pushing away from the target" — it is exactly zero restoring term, i.e. the marginal constant-energetics law `A = ε/2k_f` that the docstring itself sets up and discusses ("Without the restoring term the marginal law makes every ``k`` an equilibrium and the variance random-walks"). Running that limit is how a physicist reproduces the published marginal forcing and demonstrates the random-walk the entry claims; the guard makes it unreachable and forces the user to fake it with a huge `turnover_time`. `> 0` is the wrong relation for the stated hazard (`>= 0` rejects the genuine hazard, negative gain). Separately, `target > 0` is over-strict: I verified `VarianceController(dom; target = 0.0, turnover_time = 1.0)` is rejected even though the only thing zero `target` breaks is the DEFAULT turnover-time formula `2*float(target)/(3*_stationary_dissipation_estimate(...))` (line 559), which is bypassed when `turnover_time` is supplied — and that case is already caught by the `isfinite(tℓ)` guard two lines later. findings.title: `ConstantPower`'s public type parameters and positional-constructor arity changed

Deleting the field is right — it existed only to fill the rate array the strategy no longer uses, and the memory ledger correctly records the reduction (`tag === :power ? ZERO`). This is reported only so the surface change is on the record alongside the renames, not as a defect in the removal.

findings.title: Simulation(domain)'s default forcing mechanism replaced, changing computed trajectories for every default-configured run
findings.before: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),
findings.why_it_matters: Any caller who wrote `Simulation(domain)` (or `Simulation(; ...)`) without an explicit `velocity_forcing` — the front-door, idiomatic path the whole README and index.md example uses — now gets a materially different dynamical system: a post-step deterministic energy clamp (BandRescaling/VarianceRescaling: k pinned exactly to `target` every step) replaced by a feedback-controlled RHS term (VarianceController: k relaxes exponentially toward `target` with a settling time, and genuinely fluctuates around it). No exception is thrown; the run just produces different numbers for identical input. This is exactly the 'silently alter what the package does for input that was previously valid' case the audit is built to catch — the fix is well-justified (the old default measurably ran at first order, 1.02 vs the scheme's advertised 3.01) and the change IS documented (decision 58, the rewritten docstring note, and test/simulation_run.jl's updated `isa VarianceController` assertion), so it is announced rather than covert, but it remains the single widest computed-result change in the round and deserves being named as such rather than absorbed into a rename sweep.

findings.title: add_forcing_source! arity widened from 3 to 5 required positional arguments (exported generic function)
findings.before: add_forcing_source!(::AbstractForcing, N̂, domain::FixedDomain) = N̂
findings.after: add_forcing_source!(::AbstractForcing, N̂, field, domain::FixedDomain, diffusivity::Real) = N̂
findings.why_it_matters: `add_forcing_source!` is exported and part of the documented `AbstractForcing` extension protocol ("a strategy may implement any of ... add_forcing_source!"). Any user-defined forcing type that implemented the old 3-argument form now has a method the run never calls at all: `step!` calls the new 5-argument signature, dispatch falls through to the new do-nothing default, and the user's forcing silently stops firing — precisely the failure mode the package's own doc policy calls out ('a wrong quiet run'). The round does mitigate this: `ResolvedGenerator`'s constructor gained `_defines_stale_source_hook`, which enumerates the method table and throws an `ArgumentError` naming the offending type if it finds an old-arity override, so in practice the break is loud rather than silent. Still, this is a genuine arity change to a public generic with no back-compat shim, worth recording as a public-contract event even though it is guarded.

findings.title: Four exported public names removed outright, with no deprecation alias, across a comprehensive rename sweep
findings.before:
BandRescaling,
...
       set_forcing_rate!,
       uses_linear_rate,
       apply_forcing!,
findings.after:
VarianceRescaling,

...

findings.why_it_matters: `BandRescaling`, `apply_forcing!`, and `uses_linear_rate` are removed from the umbrella's `using`/`export` lists entirely and replaced by `VarianceRescaling`/`VarianceController`, `project_forcing!`, `uses_steady_linear_rate`. Reported here only because the lens asks for every export added/removed/renamed to be named explicitly; the renames are semantically motivated (the old names asserted 'linear' where 'steady' was the load-bearing property) and are swept consistently through docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/src/api/Forcing.md, docs/src/index.md and every test file that used them.

findings.title: ConstantPower's struct field count and positional-constructor arity changed (3 fields → 2)
findings.before:
struct ConstantPower{K, I, T} <: AbstractForcing
  band::K
  indicator::I         # the band indicator as a real array — the rate fill's factor
  injection_rate::T
end
findings.after:
struct ConstantPower{K, T} <: AbstractForcing
  band::K
  injection_rate::T    # the VALUE of the dissipation rate to hold: dissipation or scalar_dissipation
end
findings.why_it_matters: `ConstantPower` is an exported type; removing its `indicator` field changes `fieldnames(ConstantPower)` and the arity of its plain positional constructor `ConstantPower(band, indicator, injection_rate)` → `ConstantPower(band, injection_rate)`. Any external code that built the struct positionally (rather than through the documented `ConstantPower(domain; injection_rate, ...)` keyword form) would break. Severity is kept low because a repo-wide grep found no positional use anywhere in src/, test/, or docs/ — the constructor was never advertised for direct positional use per the project's own doc policy ('name the plain positional constructor only where a reader might reasonably call it') — and the removal is a real simplification (the lazy band kernel is now convolved against directly, eliminating a materialized array), not gratuitous.

findings.title: The new default forcing (VarianceController) triples per-step device synchronization and 6x's compute passes versus the old default, and the decision log recording the change never mentions this cost
findings.before: (name = "default (adaptive dt, BandRescaling :total)", cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :band_total), achieved = 3, floor = 1) — and compute model `tag === :band` -> `_ex(spectral_vector = 3)` (a flat, once-per-step cost)
findings.after: (name = "default (adaptive dt, VarianceController, 3-stage)", cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :controller, stages = 3), achieved = 10, floor = 1) — and compute model `tag === :controller` -> `_ex(spectral_vector = 6 * _evals(scheme))` = 18 passes/step on IFLowStorageRK3. `velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy)` is now what every bare `Simulation()` call gets.
findings.why_it_matters: Every user who calls the front-door `Simulation(grid_points_per_axis = ...)` with no forcing keyword — the package's own documented one-liner example — now pays 10 blocking device-to-host synchronizations and 18 field-scale reduction/convolution passes per step for the velocity forcing alone, versus 3 and 3 before: on the GPU-primary target this is exactly the axis invariant 4 ("minimal memory footprint trumps compute cost", GPU-primary) is written to protect, and it moved sharply worse for the zero-configuration case. Decision 58 in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — the narrative record of "why VarianceController is now the default" — discusses only the numerical-order motivation (1.02 to 3.01) at length and never once mentions synchronization count, pass count, or GPU cost; the only place this cost is disclosed is in code comments inside two test files, not where a reader consulting the decision log to understand the tradeoff would look.

findings.title: Decision 58's own quoted formula for the "replacement" controller is the pre-fix, buggy formula its own postscript says nearly shipped

This is a live self-contradiction inside one diff: the decision log's LaTeX was not updated when the code/docstring were corrected, which is precisely the class of defect the project's own doc policy singles out ("a plausible 'X is just Y' equivalence... false until the expansion matches").

findings.title: ConstantPower's per-step synchronization/compute cost also grew several-fold as a side effect of the same routing fix, compounding across every state-dependent forcing in the module

    whole-field ``k`` — which is what makes this calibration legitimate.   (src/SimulationRun.jl:203–205)
findings.why_it_matters: "Guarantees" described an exact per-step projection; "does" is asserted of a mechanism that only relaxes exponentially, and the strength of the claim is unchanged in the reader's eye. The commit's own oracle shows the difference is material: test/simulation_run.jl asserts `isapprox(k, k_target; rtol = 0.05)` only after 200 steps, and needs 600 steps to reach `rtol = 0.1` when started from k₀ = 0.4. The qualification exists — decision 58's amendment to decision 15 says "the controller holds it to a tolerance rather than exactly" — but it was written into the decision log and not onto the user-facing surface where the precondition for κ_max·η self-consistency is stated. A user calibrating a run reads the docstring, not §11.

Nine excess crossings on the default path are absorbed by the pre-existing `HOST_SIDE_FORCING_SCALARS` holder, whose text was not touched and describes a single scalar per forcing — "A forcing reduces its band observable (or the noise variance) to a Julia scalar, branches on it, and feeds it back to a kernel as a coefficient" — not three reductions at every stage. `ALL_HOLDERS` and `OPEN_LOCAL_WINS = ()` are byte-identical to base. So the largest gap in the ledger was created and simultaneously certified by widening an existing claim rather than writing a holder for it, which is the shape the register's two-directional rule was built to catch. Whether the 3.3× default-path sync cost is an acceptable price for the order restoration is a user decision; the instrument was adjusted so the question is never asked.

findings.title: The Simulation docstring both admits and denies that the default forcing 'really holds' k, three paragraphs apart
findings.before:
!!! note "The default holds the kinetic energy fixed, so it is not a measurable of the default run"
    `BandRescaling` is a deterministic clamp: it rescales the band every step to hold the kinetic
    energy at the target **value** … One precondition: the choice is self-consistent only if the run really holds ``k`` at `kinetic_energy`, which the front door's `BandRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees and `:band` does not.
findings.after:
!!! note "The default drives the kinetic energy to a set value, so read it as a control target"
    `VarianceController` restores ``k`` exponentially to `kinetic_energy` … It does not *impose* the value step by step as a rescale does, so the fluctuation it leaves is genuine — but it is a controlled variable's fluctuation, with the gain setting its amplitude. … One precondition: the choice is self-consistent only if the run really holds ``k`` at `kinetic_energy`. The default `VarianceController` does — its restoring term measures the whole-field ``k`` — which is what makes this calibration legitimate.
findings.why_it_matters: The note admonition (correctly, honestly) says the controller leaves a genuine fluctuation and does not impose the value — i.e. k is not exactly held. Three sentences later, in the same docstring, the grid-mode precondition asserts flatly that the run 'really holds k' and that this 'makes the calibration legitimate', dropping the fluctuation/tolerance caveat entirely. This directly contradicts ARCHITECTURE.md's own decision-58 postscript to decision 15, added in this same round: 'the controller holds it to a tolerance rather than exactly.' The identical overclaim ('the default forcing holds k at that value') is repeated verbatim in docs/src/index.md's quick-start comment (was: 'the default forcing is a deterministic clamp on k'). A grid-mode user reading only the constructor docstring — the natural, and likely only, place they look — is told the κ_max_η self-consistency guarantee is exact, as it genuinely was under the old `BandRescaling(:total)` default, when under the new default it is only an approximate, gain-and-turnover-time-dependent control-loop steady state.

findings.title: VarianceController's new docstring omits the empty-band zero-amplitude caveat its sibling ConstantPower documents for the identical hazard
findings.before: (no prior docstring; `VarianceController` is new in this diff)
findings.after: VarianceController(; target, gain = 1.0, turnover_time = nothing, lowest_shell = 1, highest_shell = 2) … [no note on band emptiness anywhere in its docstring, though its `add_forcing_source!` contains: `amplitude = _band_is_empty(band_variance) ? 0.0 : (dissipation - restoring) / (2 * band_variance)`]
findings.why_it_matters: ConstantPower's docstring (same file, same round) carries the admonition '!!! note "An empty band is left alone, not driven infinitely hard" … a scalar seeded with nothing in the forced shells … the rate is set to zero instead, so an empty band stays empty rather than receiving an unbounded kick.' VarianceController's `add_forcing_source!` implements the exact same `_band_is_empty` guard against the same divide-by-zero, but its docstring — the one a reader consults to pick a forcing, and the package's new default — says nothing about it. A user forcing a passive scalar with `VarianceController` from a zero-initial-variance state (a real configuration per the project's own warm-up research memory) gets silent zero forcing with no documented explanation, exactly the 'silent NaN/silent no-op' failure mode the rest of the codebase is careful to call out.
